questions.question: Describe the pastoral way of life of the Khoikhoi.
questions.expected_answer: The Khoikhoi lived mainly by herding fat-tailed sheep, long-horned cattle and later goats. Milk was their main food, and animals were killed mainly on special occasions. Animals also gave skins, fat and transport. They moved with the seasons to find grass and water, and also hunted, gathered and made clay pots.

questions.question: Describe a Khoikhoi house and explain why it suited their way of life.
questions.expected_answer: It was a dome of bent wooden poles covered with mats woven from reeds or rushes. It was cool in summer and kept the rain out in winter. It suited a moving life because it could be taken apart quickly, rolled up and carried on pack oxen to the next grazing place.

questions.question: Give two ways the San and Khoikhoi cooperated and two reasons they came into conflict.
questions.expected_answer: They traded meat, skins and beads for milk and animals; some San worked for Khoikhoi as herders or hunters; and they intermarried. They clashed because herds ate the grass and drank the water that wild animals needed, herders took over waterholes, and San hunters sometimes killed herders' animals.
